The Ford Focus family

4 generations and variants in the Index, 2000–2018. Oldest first; every card opens the full page, with its own versions, figures and story.

  1. 2000–2007

    Ford Focus (first generation, North America)

    The world car that actually worked: Europe's best handler became America's best-selling small car — 286,166 in year 1 — and the SVT Focus gave the US a real hot hatch.

    130 hp8.5 sec 0-60118 mph top1,822,361 built
    ZX3 2.0 Zetec · 2.0 SPI (base) · SVT Focus (2002–04) · 2.0 Duratec (2005–07)
  2. 2008–2011

    Ford Focus (second generation, North America)

    America's placeholder Focus: old bones, new chrome, a 2-door coupe nobody asked for — and Sync, the voice-controlled tech that mattered more than the car around it.

    140 hp8.5 sec 0-60110 mph top704,394 built
    Sedan · Coupe (2008–10)
  3. 2012–2018

    Ford Focus (third generation)

    The global Focus at its peak — the world's best-selling car in 2012 — undone in America by a dual-clutch gearbox that shuddered its reputation away.

    160 hp8.0 sec 0-60118 mph top1,356,303 built
    2.0 GDI · 1.0 EcoBoost (2015–18) · Focus ST (2013–18) · Focus Electric (2012–18)
  4. 2016–2018

    Ford Focus RS (Mk3)

    350 hp, all-wheel drive, a manual, and a button labeled Drift Mode: the first RS America was ever allowed to buy hit 60 in 4.6 seconds and left after 3 years.

    350 hp4.6 sec 0-60165 mph top
    Focus RS · 2018 RS Limited Edition
